archetype.name: Bubble Team (power-play-powered)
archetype.definition: A club whose winning record rests on a league-best power play and elite finishing, while it is out-chanced at 5-on-5 and leaky in goal, which leaves it in the playoff mix without being on solid ground.

report.headline: The power play is winning games that 5-on-5 hockey and the goaltending keep giving back
report.take:
Anaheim at 10-7-1 is a team with two very different faces. With the man advantage it is the best unit in the league: a 38.5% power play, ranked first, against a league average of 22.5%. At 5-on-5 it gets 44.2% of the expected goals, 28th in the league, and ranks 29th in shots on goal a game at 24.9. The offense still ranks 4th by goals per game at 3.83, because its skaters convert at a 15.4% clip in all situations, second in the league, against a league mark of 11.6%. Defensively it allows 3.67 goals a game, 30th, behind a team save percentage of .869, 31st. The net result is a goal differential of +0.17 a game, a site rank of 17th and fourth place in the Pacific.

The forward core is driving almost all of it. Cutter Gauthier has 15 goals on 72 shots and sits 4th on the left-wing tab. Leo Carlsson has 26 points, 17 of them on the power play. Beckett Sennecke has 22 points and Jackson LaCombe, who plays 27.35 minutes a night, has 22. Of the listed forwards' 122 points, 58 came on the power play. That is the real engine of this team, and it is also its main exposure: a power play converting at nearly 40% and a shooting percentage this far above the league will both come down. Most of the forwards' individual expected-goal shares are under 50%, Granlund's at .362 the lowest, so the even-strength play is not covering for anything.

What the record does not hide is luck in close games. Pts vs Goal Diff is +0.2, so the standings points match the goals. The 5-on-5 PDO is 99.9, which means the hot finishing is a special-teams and all-situations story, not a 5-on-5 bounce. The bigger worry is that 5-on-5 has slipped badly. Last season this team had a 51.9% xGF and went 43-33-6 to reach the playoffs. It already allowed goals at a rate ranked 29th then, so the leaky defense is not new, but the territorial edge that offset it is gone.

The November surge, 5-0 with 26 goals scored and 16 allowed, is real points in the bank after a 5-8 October that included a five-game losing streak. It also came on 5.2 goals a game, a scoring rate nothing in the shot data supports. The direction of travel is a team that stays in the bubble conversation. As the power play cools it will need the goaltending, at .869, to climb back toward normal, and that is the one regression likely to work in its favor.

strengths.title: A league-best power play
strengths.body: At 38.5% the power play ranks first and runs well above the league average. It is fueled by Carlsson, Gauthier, Sennecke and LaCombe, who all carry double-digit power-play points. The unit is clearly good, since last year's rate was 18.6%, but no power play holds a rate like this over a full season, so expect a strong unit rather than a historic one.

strengths.title: Top-six finishing talent
strengths.body: Gauthier's 15 goals on 72 shots and his 4th place on the left-wing tab headline a group graded B, with Sennecke and Carlsson also in the top 20 at their positions. The team's 15.4% shooting, second in the league, partly reflects real shooting skill at the top of the lineup. It is still far enough above the league rate that some of it is heat.

strengths.title: Wins earned on the scoreboard
strengths.body: The record is not propped up by overtime or one-goal luck. Pts vs Goal Diff is a neutral +0.2, and the team is +3 in goal differential. The November run included lopsided wins over Ottawa, Calgary and Pittsburgh. Whatever regression comes will come through the shooting and the power play, not through close-game coin flips.

concerns.title: Out-chanced badly at 5-on-5
concerns.body: A 44.2% xGF ranks 28th, and only 24.9 shots on goal a game ranks 29th, so the team rarely controls play at even strength. That is a sharp fall from last season's 51.9% xGF. When the power play and the shooting cool, this is what the record will rest on, and right now it would not hold up a winning team.

concerns.title: Goaltending near the league floor
concerns.body: The listed goalies stop .869 of shots together, and the team save percentage ranks 31st. Dostal has made 10 of the starts at .866 with a -1.4 GSAx, and the group grades a D. Shots against are close to league average at 27.1 a game, so this is mostly about the saves, which should rebound somewhat. Last season's -12.8 GSAx says not to count on a full recovery.

concerns.title: Soft penalty kill, porous defense
concerns.body: The penalty kill at 73% ranks 23rd. Opposing forwards are scoring above their own averages against this team, which ranks 29th on that measure. LaCombe plays 27.35 minutes on the top pair with a .38 xGF share, and a C+ blueline is being asked to do more than it can.

trend.note: A 5-8 October, including a five-game losing streak, gave way to a 5-0 November start that pushed the record to 10-8 in regulation terms. The climb came on unsustainable scoring of 5.2 goals a game rather than better shot share.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games against penalty kills built to stop it
weekAhead.body:
All three games are at home: Nashville on Wednesday, the Islanders on Saturday and Calgary on Sunday. The common thread is the power play running into good penalty kills. Nashville kills 88.5% (3rd) and New York 85.7% (5th), and both have A- goaltending, with GSAx of 6.9 and 8.2. Those two games are where Anaheim's model gets tested, because neither opponent leaks goals: Nashville ranks 6th in defense and holds wingers well under their averages.

Calgary is the softer end of the week. The Flames rank 28th in offense and 25th in defense, grade a D in goal and sit 23rd on the site, and Anaheim beat them 5-3 on the road a week ago. Calgary's +2.5 Pts vs Goal Diff says its record already flatters it. Neither New York (24th) nor Calgary scores much, which gives Anaheim's goaltending a chance to steady. Two of three looks like a fair return; a sweep would need the power play to keep beating elite kills.

keyMatchups.title: Power play vs Nashville's kill
keyMatchups.body: Anaheim's first-ranked power play meets a Nashville penalty kill ranked 3rd at 88.5%, backed by goalies 6th in GSAx. Nashville's defense ranks 6th and holds wingers the third-furthest under their averages, a bad sign for Gauthier and Sennecke at even strength. If the power play is shut down here, Anaheim's 5-on-5 deficit decides the game.

keyMatchups.title: Islanders' hot goaltending
keyMatchups.body: New York's goalies are 4th in GSAx at 8.2 and its kill is 5th. Its offense ranks 24th and its power play 29th at 14.6%, so Anaheim's weak penalty kill should be spared. Expect a low-event game; the Islanders won the October meeting 3-2.

keyMatchups.title: Calgary's weak offense and goaltending
keyMatchups.body: Calgary ranks 28th in offense, shoots 9.3% and has D-graded goaltending with a -4.2 GSAx. It is the best chance all week for Anaheim's skaters to pile up goals at 5-on-5 and for Dostal to post a clean night. Calgary does allow centers points above their averages, which favors Carlsson and Granlund.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Anaheim can win the Nashville and Islanders games if the power play goes quiet against two top-five penalty kills.

restOfSeason.body:
The current pace of 46 wins and 96 points is built on a 38.5% power play and 15.4% shooting, and both will come down. A 44.2% xGF at 5-on-5 is the bigger long-run problem, because it suggests this team gets outplayed most nights at even strength. Working the other way, a .869 save percentage is close to the bottom of the league and should improve with volume, even if the goaltending stays below average as it was last year.

The net is a team that drifts toward the middle: still a top-ten offense because the top six and the power play are genuinely good, still a bottom-third defense, and in a Pacific race where it can make up ground on Seattle but is unlikely to catch Edmonton or Vegas. Expect something in the 86-94 point range. The deciding factor is whether the 5-on-5 play climbs back toward last season's level.
swingFactors: How far the power play falls from its 38.5% rate
Recovering a 5-on-5 shot share near last season's

confidence.note: 18 games is a small sample, and the drivers (power-play and shooting rates) are the kind that move a lot.
